faq.a: Rabotka's hiring space for organisations: companies, NGOs, schools, health facilities, public bodies. You publish your jobs, receive and sort applications, run your interviews and decide as a team, all in one place. Your jobs reach Rabotka's candidates in your country, and your careers page receives applications from everywhere else.

faq.q: What can I do with Rabotka Business?
faq.a: Write and publish a job in minutes, receive applications and follow them step by step, have CVs read and ranked for a role, get the contact details of the candidates you're interested in, offer video or in-person interviews with a report to share, and work together with your recruiters and reviewers. The details depend on your plan.

faq.q: Can I import CVs from Gmail?
faq.a: Yes. Connect your Gmail inbox once, read-only: you see recent emails that contain a CV, tick the ones to analyse, and only those attachments are read. No email is kept or sent, and you can disconnect Gmail at any time. You can also upload PDFs, Word files or photos of CVs from your device.

faq.q: Can I post my jobs on LinkedIn?
faq.a: Yes. Connect your LinkedIn account once from a job: it is posted on your profile as a card, with ready-made text you review and the image of your choice. The card opens your careers page, where candidates apply; their applications are flagged as coming from LinkedIn. Each recruiter on the team posts on their own profile.

You choose the role — one of your jobs or a role described for the occasion — then the CVs. Rabotka reads each CV, compares it with the role and gives it a score out of 100, with its strengths, points to watch and a reading of the career path. The ranking is ready in minutes; a notification lets you know.
PDFs, Word files (.docx) and photos or scans (JPG, PNG, WEBP), uploaded from your device or picked straight from your Gmail inbox. A file that can't be read, or that isn't a CV, isn't counted.

faq.q: What does Rabotka do in my mailbox?
faq.a: Nothing more than what you ask. The connection is read-only: you see recent emails that contain a CV, tick the ones to analyse, and only those attachments are read. No email is kept or sent, and you can disconnect your mailbox at any time.
The files and contact details of analysed CVs are deleted automatically at the end of the period shown when you run the analysis. The scores and the ranking remain available.

faq.q: How does a video interview work?
faq.a: When you offer the interview, create a video link: the call takes place in Rabotka, with nothing to install. The candidate joins from their invitation, on a computer or a phone, without an account. You can invite a colleague or a manager: they get their own link by email and join under their name. You can also paste a Meet or Zoom link if you prefer.

During or after the interview, take your notes: type or dictate them. In a Rabotka video call, the interview is transcribed automatically, sentence by sentence, and everyone can see that it is. From your notes and the transcript, Rabotka writes a report: summary, strengths, points to watch, practical details and next steps. You review it, edit it, email it to your team or save it as a PDF. Neither the sound nor the picture of the call is recorded.

faq.q: Do interviews show up in my calendar?
faq.a: Yes. Add your interview calendar link once to Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar: each interview shows up there and updates on its own, whether it is confirmed, moved or cancelled.

faq.q: Which organisations can open a business account?
faq.a: Companies of any size, start-ups, cooperatives and economic interest groups, schools and training centres, NGOs, associations and foundations, health facilities, public administrations, public institutions and international organisations.

They depend on your country and status: trade register entry (such as the RCCM) and tax number for a company, registration receipt and articles for an association or NGO, operating licence or accreditation for a school or health facility, founding act for a public body. The form tells you exactly which documents are expected.

faq.q: How do I sign in to the business space?
faq.a: With the account's email address: a one-time code is sent each time you sign in. No password to manage.

rediger-une-offre-qui-attire.title: Writing a job post that attracts the right candidates
rediger-une-offre-qui-attire.description: Title, duties, conditions: what makes a qualified candidate apply, and what drives them away.

sections.heading: A title candidates search for
paragraphs: Candidates type a trade, not the role's internal name. “Cashier” finds more people than “Checkout host level 2”. Keep the title short and precise, with the trade first.

sections.heading: Duties before profile
paragraphs: Start by describing what the person will do day to day, in a few concrete lines. The profile you're looking for comes next: the skills that are really needed, not a wish list.
list: Three to five main duties, with action verbs
Essential skills, separate from the “nice to have”
Location, hours and contract type right at the start

sections.heading: Drop what wrongly rules people out
paragraphs: Age, sex or family situation have no place in a job post, and keep competent candidates away. Rabotka removes these criteria when it writes the job post for you.

sections.heading: One question to save time
paragraphs: A well-chosen screening question (“Do you have a truck licence?”) sorts better than a long text. Make it a knock-out question only if the answer is truly blocking.

trier-des-dizaines-de-cv.title: Sorting dozens of CVs without spending the day on it
trier-des-dizaines-de-cv.description: A three-step method to go from a pile of CVs to a shortlist, with CV analysis.

sections.heading: 1. Describe the role before reading
paragraphs: Before opening a single CV, write down what really matters: relevant experience, essential skills, the city. This is the text CV analysis compares with each candidate.

sections.heading: 2. Let Rabotka do the first read
paragraphs: Drop all the CVs at once, or pick them from your Gmail inbox. Each one is read, scored out of 100 and comes with its strengths and points to watch.
list: Start with the highest scores, but read the “why”
Look at the points to watch: missing information isn't a flaw
Keep a second list for unusual profiles

sections.heading: 3. Decide between the last few
paragraphs: Compare up to 5 CVs side by side and ask your questions: “Which one has already managed a team?”. Export the ranking as a PDF to share it with the hiring manager.

organiser-ses-entretiens.title: Scheduling interviews without endless back-and-forth
organiser-ses-entretiens.description: Offer your slots, run the video call, share the report: an interview that really serves the decision.

sections.heading: Offer, don't negotiate
paragraphs: Offer a precise time, or up to three to choose from, with the format (on site, phone or video) and the place. The candidate picks, confirms or asks for another time from their email: no back-and-forth. For a video interview, create the link in Rabotka: the call happens there, with nothing to install.

sections.heading: The same questions for everyone
paragraphs: To compare candidates, ask them the same main questions, tied to the role's duties. Write down the answers during the interview or right after, while they're fresh: typed or dictated, beside the video call.
list: A question about a situation they've already faced
A question about a difficulty of the role

sections.heading: Decide together
paragraphs: Invite the hiring manager into the call: they join with their own link, without an account. After the interview, Rabotka writes the report from your notes; review it and send it to the team. Each member gives their opinion (Yes, Maybe, No): the decision is made on shared facts, and the hired candidate gets their contract right away.
